documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs
documents.title: AI Use Guidelines
documents.summary: A short hub page that frames Ball State's GenAI guidelines as living and lists separate guidelines for instructors, research, administration, misuse and students (the linked texts were not accessible). The only substantive rule is for students: use GenAI only as the instructor's selected GenAI Statement allows, and complete two self-check steps first.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university-wide stance. It tells students they 'must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course' and that the self-checkers do not 'mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment', so the decision is handed to instructors and assignments.

units.why: The page states its purpose: guidelines to help the community use GenAI 'responsibly and ethically'. This is an institution-level framing of purpose and scope (P56), not a rule on a specific use.
units.anchor: help our community use Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools responsibly and ethically
units.frag_start: Ball State University has established the following
units.frag_end: as they engage in their work

units.why: 'living guidelines ... continuously updated ... subject to change' says the policy is provisional and will be revised, which is P54; the email address invites feedback.
units.anchor: These are living guidelines and are continuously updated as new information is received.
units.frag_end: All information is subject to change.

units.why: 'students are encouraged to complete Step 1 ... Step 2' asks students to run self-check tools before using GenAI for coursework. P10 is about asking the instructor, which is different, and no other type covers a pre-use self-check, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to complete
units.frag_start: If generative AI use is permitted, students
units.frag_end: before using GenAI tools for coursework.
units.policy: If generative AI use is permitted, students are encouraged to complete Step 1 (Should I use AI?) and Step 2 (How should I use AI responsibly?) before using GenAI tools for coursework.
units.uncovered_note: Students are encouraged to complete two self-check tools (Should I use AI? / How should I use AI responsibly?) before using GenAI for coursework.

units.why: 'does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment' leaves permission to be decided assignment by assignment. P04 fits (per-assignment decision); P11 does not because it is about checkers, not carry-over between courses.
units.anchor: Completion of the checkers does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment.

units.why: 'Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course' binds students to whatever statement the instructor picked; the university sets no rule itself. That is P04 (instructor sets the rule), with the syllabus statement as the vehicle.
units.anchor: Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course

units.why: 'assignment-specific directions' must be followed as well, so permissions can differ assignment by assignment and are not set once per course. P04 (per-assignment rule) is chosen over P11 since nothing is said about carry-over.
units.anchor: assignment-specific directions, instructors' guidance
units.policy: Students follow assignment-specific directions and instructors' guidance on GenAI.

units.why: Students must also follow the Student Academic Ethics Policy, which brings AI conduct under the integrity process. P36 is the closest type but the sentence only points to the policy and adds no sanction rule.
units.anchor: Student Academic Ethics Policy
units.policy: Students follow Ball State University's Student Academic Ethics Policy when using GenAI for coursework.

documents.title: AI Guidelines (AI Initiatives)
documents.summary: The IT office sets out seven institutional AI values and then rules on approved tools, meetings, data classification, retention, sustainability and citation, before repeating the provost's guideline hub. It welcomes AI optimistically but leaves permission in coursework to instructor statements.
documents.stance_why: The page says the university is 'optimistic about AI' and urges approved tools, but for coursework it repeats that 'students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected', so it sets no course-level stance and delegates to instructors.

units.why: 'we are optimistic about AI' while acknowledging challenges is an institution-level framing of principles (P56), not a rule on use.
units.anchor: While we are optimistic about AI, we understand that these technologies bring

units.why: Excellence value: 'commit to using AI in ways that align with and uphold our Academic Integrity Policy'. A value that sets the framework (P56); it does not itself classify misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: We commit to using AI in ways that align with and uphold our

units.why: Innovation value: 'commit to responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance creativity, learning, and research' welcomes AI experimentation, so P02 (welcome/encourage) with encourage stance.
units.anchor: We commit to responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance creativity, learning, and research.

units.why: Courage value: 'addressing potential ethical challenges and risks' names ethical risk of AI as something to address, which is P53.
units.anchor: willingly exploring the possibilities within AI while also addressing potential ethical challenges and risks

units.why: Integrity value: 'upholding human creativity and critical thinking with our AI usage, avoiding misuse' keeps humans as the thinkers, matching P32 (AI must not replace thinking).
units.anchor: upholding human creativity and critical thinking with our AI usage, avoiding misuse

units.why: Inclusiveness value: 'developing and using AI in accessible and equitable ways' concerns equity and access (P51).
units.anchor: developing and using AI in accessible and equitable ways

units.why: Social responsibility value: 'minimizing harm ... prioritizing ethical considerations when using AI' names harms and ethics (P53).
units.anchor: We commit to minimizing harm, maintaining rigorous standards, and prioritizing ethical considerations

units.why: 'living guidelines ... subject to change' says the guidelines are provisional (P54).
units.anchor: These are living guidelines and are continuously updated as new information is received.
units.frag_end: All information is subject to change.

units.why: 'students are encouraged to complete Step 1 ... Step 2' asks for a pre-use self-check. P10 (ask the instructor) does not fit and no other type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to complete
units.frag_start: If generative AI use is permitted, students
units.frag_end: before using GenAI tools for coursework.
units.policy: If generative AI use is permitted, students are encouraged to complete Step 1 (Should I use AI?) and Step 2 (How should I use AI responsibly?) before using GenAI tools for coursework.
units.uncovered_note: Students are encouraged to complete two self-check tools before using GenAI for coursework.

units.why: 'does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment' leaves permission to each assignment (P04).
units.anchor: Completion of the checkers does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment.

units.why: 'Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected' hands the rule to the instructor's statement (P04).
units.anchor: Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course

units.why: 'Highly encouraged to use University-approved AI tools' recommends vetted tools for everyone, which is P50 (prefer vetted tools); the tools are university-provided but nothing names a specific tool, so P17 is not chosen.
units.anchor: Ball State students, faculty, and staff are highly encouraged to use
units.policy: Ball State students, faculty, and staff are highly encouraged to use University-approved AI tools.

units.why: 'Before purchasing any AI tools ... not from the University ... please submit a request to the Technology HelpDesk' asks users to consult IT before buying non-university tools, consistent with preferring vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: Before purchasing any AI tools or services that are not from the University
units.policy: Before purchasing AI tools or services not from the University or its partners, users submit a request to the Technology HelpDesk or call to discuss their intended use.

units.why: 'Faculty and staff at Ball State must utilize university-approved AI tools in virtual meetings' is a requirement on employees' tool choice, matching P50 (vetted tools).
units.anchor: Faculty and staff at Ball State must utilize university-approved AI tools in virtual meetings.

units.why: 'employees and students need to use the built-in AI Companion features provided in Zoom and Microsoft Teams' names sanctioned tools for meeting transcription and summaries (P17).
units.anchor: need to use the built-in AI Companion features provided in Zoom and Microsoft Teams

units.why: 'Third-party tools such as otter.ai or read.ai are not permitted' bans unvetted tools because of 'data security and privacy risks', so P50 (privacy, vetted tools).
units.anchor: Third-party tools such as otter.ai or read.ai are not permitted

units.why: Zoom and Teams transcription is 'not a replacement for full ADA-compliant, human-generated captions': an accessibility limit on AI. P51 (access, accommodations) is closest.
units.anchor: not a replacement for full ADA-compliant, human-generated captions

units.why: 'you're only allowed to upload: Public Data' for personal and basic accounts limits what data may go into AI, a data-protection rule (P50) rather than P49, which is about course materials.
units.anchor: you're only allowed to upload
units.policy: With personal and basic accounts accessed through the Ball State login, only Public Data may be uploaded to AI platforms.

units.why: Accounts with advanced AI models and Ball State login 'are permitted to upload Public, Internal, or Restricted Data': a permission tied to the vetted-account tier of data (P50).
units.anchor: you are permitted to upload Public, Internal, or Restricted Data
units.policy: With an advanced AI account (Gemini Pro, GPT Team, Copilot) with Ball State login activated, Public, Internal, or Restricted Data may be uploaded.

units.why: 'Critical data ... is never to be uploaded to AI tools' is an absolute ban on certain personal and confidential data (P50).
units.anchor: is never to be uploaded to AI tools
units.frag_end: never to be uploaded to AI tools.
units.policy: Critical data, including HIPAA-protected patient data, social security numbers, credit card and banking information, and passport or driver's license information, is never uploaded to AI tools.

units.why: 'external AI tools, like Gemini and ChatGPT, may store your data' warns about retention and disclaims responsibility for personal data: facts about AI tools storing prompts (P50).
units.anchor: external AI tools, like Gemini and ChatGPT, may store your data
units.frag_end: personal data stored on external AI tools.

units.why: 'We recognize the energy consumption and resource demands required to power AI' names the environmental cost of AI (P53).
units.anchor: We recognize the energy consumption and resource demands required to power AI.

units.why: 'We will incorporate environmental principles and environmentally responsible practices' into AI efforts is an institutional commitment on environmental harm (P53).
units.anchor: We will incorporate environmental principles and environmentally responsible practices

units.why: 'If AI is used in academic research, it must be appropriately cited following MLA, APA, or Chicago' is a research-specific citation rule. P62 (research and scholarship) fits better than P24 because it is scoped to research.
units.anchor: If AI is used in academic research, it must be appropriately cited
units.policy: If AI is used in academic research, it must be appropriately cited following MLA, APA, or Chicago style guidelines.

units.why: 'we recommend being upfront about AI usage when creating draft documents, emails, records, and files' recommends disclosing AI use in work products (P24, should).
units.anchor: we recommend being upfront about AI usage when creating draft documents, emails, records, and files

units.why: The template 'This document contains AI content from [PLATFORM] [MODEL] generated on [DATE]. AI was used to [INTENT]' requires tool, model, date and purpose in the citation, which is P25.
units.anchor: This document contains AI content from
units.policy: The recommended citation states the platform, the model, the date generated, and what AI was used to do.

units.why: 'using AI tools to complete assignments and claiming it as your own work is a direct violation of ... Academic Integrity Policy' forbids submitting AI-produced work as one's own. Chosen P19 over P36 because the core is the banned act; the misconduct label is secondary.
units.anchor: using AI tools to complete assignments and claiming it as your own work

units.why: 'Faculty are required to report violations to the Office of the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs' binds instructors to report AI integrity violations, a misconduct-handling rule (P36).
units.anchor: Faculty are required to report violations to the Office of the Vice Provost

units.why: 'foster ongoing critical reflection' with reflection questions on social and environmental impact asks users to reflect on the broader impact of AI use, a responsible-use concern (P53).
units.anchor: We aim to foster ongoing critical reflection.

documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost, Student Services
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: The integrity page describes the reporting and hearing process for academic ethics violations and, in a few places, ties it to AI: syllabus expectations for generative AI, a misuse guideline, citing AI, and AI-use scales. Most process rules are generic to all integrity cases and apply to AI misuse.
documents.stance_why: The page does not ban or allow AI. It asks faculty to 'make explicit on your syllabi' their expectations on generative AI and points to scales 'for communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use', so the decision rests with instructors.

units.why: The page opens by saying the Vice Provost's office 'is responsible for the overall administration of the Student Academic Ethics policy', the policy under which AI misuse is handled. Governance of the integrity regime (P56).
units.anchor: is responsible for the overall administration of the Student Academic Ethics policy
units.frag_start: Office of the Vice Provost of

units.why: Step 1 has the instructor request a 'preliminary inquiry meeting', citing the AI misuse guidelines. Talking with the student before any formal allegation is P57. The process is generic to integrity cases and covers AI misuse.
units.anchor: instructor and student meet to discuss incident before instructor determines whether a formal allegation
units.frag_end: Instructor should consult with unit-level leadership before proceeding to next step.

units.why: The instructor 'may propose resolutions up to and including: Failure in the course and academic ethics education sanction' states the range of penalties in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Instructor may propose resolutions up to and including: Failure in the course

units.why: The student can send 'a statement indicating disagreement ... along with up to five pages summarizing why they deny the allegation', i.e. a right to respond, which is P64.
units.anchor: a statement indicating disagreement with allegation and/or resolution, along with up to five pages

units.why: 'If there are multiple offenses ... Suspension, Expulsion, Revocation of degree' states escalating penalties by offense (P37).
units.anchor: If there are multiple offenses
units.policy: If there are multiple offenses, this may involve formal resolution and/or additional penalties, including suspension, expulsion, and revocation of degree.

units.why: The hearing panel gives student and faculty 'up to 30 minutes to present relevant information to the panel', a fair chance to present evidence (P64).
units.anchor: Have up to 30 minutes to present relevant information to the panel

units.why: Faculty are advised to 'make explicit on your syllabi ... your expectations regarding ... using generative AI (for the entire course or for specific assignments)'. This is an AI statement in the syllabus (P09); the course-vs-assignment scope is secondary.
units.anchor: Make explicit on your syllabi and discuss with students your expectations
units.policy: Instructors make explicit on their syllabi, and discuss with students, their expectations about acceptable and unacceptable actions, including using generative AI for the entire course or for specific assignments.

units.why: 'Use authentic assignments that are unique to the course student learning outcomes and refresh often' is advice on assignment design to prevent dishonesty; the page elsewhere frames it as part of the AI response ('authentic assessment'). P35 (redesign assignments).
units.anchor: authentic assignments that are unique to the course student learning outcomes and refresh often

units.why: Students are told to 'Know when AI tools are permissible and how to properly cite them', which puts the onus on students to learn what is allowed and cite AI. Citation of AI is P24.
units.anchor: Know when AI tools are permissible and how to properly cite them.

units.why: The Student Generative AI Use Scale and the AI Assessment Scale are recommended 'for communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use', i.e. named levels of use (P05), offered to instructors.
units.anchor: communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use

units.why: 'AI can enable and disrupt learning for many students' is the page's framing of why AI matters for integrity and assessment: a general statement of the issue rather than a rule (P56).
units.anchor: AI can enable and disrupt learning for many students
units.frag_end: meaningful engagement, we offer a few helpful resources.

notes: The detailed instructor, research, administrative and misuse guidelines sit behind an inaccessible SharePoint link, so only the hub text was coded. The IT and provost hub text overlaps and each was coded on its own. Academic integrity process steps are generic to all violations; only those that bear on AI misuse (preliminary meeting, penalty range, right to respond) were coded. No computing-unit or school-level policy exists in the collect file.
